about: Numbers for the current version of Alcaraz (ATP only): the previous version averaged with a second, all-tier model, equal weights on log-odds fixed in advance. Every value is copied from the research result files named under provenance (hash-pinned in docs/benchmarks/sources.json); nothing here is recomputed. Differences are left minus right; negative favours the left side. Contrast blocks keep the scorer's own layout: difference and scores per metric, interval_95_block8 the primary 95% interval (stationary calendar-week bootstrap, mean block eight weeks, 5,000 draws), interval_95_block4_log_loss and interval_95_block13_log_loss the block-length checks, annual_log_loss the per-season differences.

versions.current: Alcaraz, the current version: sigma(0.5 logit(previous) + 0.5 logit(second_model)) for every match; no refit and no weight fitted on test data.
versions.previous: The previous version of Alcaraz: the boosted model with lower-tier history and the entry-status block, unchanged.
versions.second_model: The second model: gradient boosting on an all-tier match table from 1991 (tour, qualifying, Challenger and Futures), trained on tour, qualifying and Challenger matches, three training windows (8, 12, 16 seasons) averaged in log-odds.

names.buildoak_fair: BuildOak (github.com/buildoak/tennis-xgboost-autoresearch) on the same lower-tier files and the same timing rule as Alcaraz (results visible two days after the match, no future-dated settings).
names.buildoak_native_lower_tier: BuildOak on the same lower-tier files with its own native setup (results used at once, lower-tier results dated on the Sunday of their week).
names.buildoak_two_day_rule_only: As buildoak_fair, with only the timing change applied.
names.buildoak_released: BuildOak as released: its own main-tour data and its own native setup.
names.buildoak_main_tour_fair: BuildOak on main-tour data only, with the fair timing rule.
names.catboost_walk_forward: hikmatazimzade/tennis-ai's CatBoost recipe, refitted for each season on the author's own feature table.
names.catboost_lower_tier: The same CatBoost recipe given the lower-tier files Alcaraz uses.
names.catboost_shipped_checkpoint: The CatBoost checkpoint the author ships, on 2025.
names.catboost_shipped_refit: The same recipe refitted through 2024, on 2025.
names.stack_without_lookahead: yaobviously/tennis_elo's ridge and LightGBM stack, rerun from the author's notebook with its look-ahead removed.
names.alcaraz: In the stack and shipped-CatBoost blocks the left side is named alcaraz; the block's key (current or previous) says which version it is.

ladder_2017_2025.about: Identical priced ATP matches, 2017-2025; match-level bootstrap stratified by year (interval). Rungs: elo, atp_p0, atp_full_tier, previous, current, pinnacle_normalised. The atp_p1 rung was not rerun on this pass; its values on the same matches are in docs/ladder.json.

fair_buildoak.about: Alcaraz against BuildOak on the same lower-tier files and timing rule. corrected: the 2025 pass with the selection-label defect fixed (run after the registered result was seen). registered: the pre-registered pass, whose 2025 second-model settings were chosen on a file with 2024's results blanked. 2017-2024 is identical in both.

y2017_2024.about: The registered 2017-2024 pass that put BuildOak on the fair timing rule; also measures what BuildOak's native setup was worth to it. y2024 is the 2024 season alone; y2017_2023 the seasons before it.

y2014_2016.about: Seasons on which none of these forecasts had been scored before. The current version can be formed only for 2015-2016 (the previous version's lineage needs six warm-up seasons); the second model alone reaches 2014.

buildoak_released.about: BuildOak as released, run with its own main-tour data and native setup, on the same 2017-2025 matches (corrected 2025 file).

baselines.about: Five Elo and ranking baselines on the same 2017-2025 matches: FiveThirtyEight surface Elo, pooled Elo with K 32, Kovalchik's overall Elo with a major-tournament adjustment, a ranking logistic and weighted Elo (WElo).

catboost_walk_forward.about: hikmatazimzade/tennis-ai's CatBoost refitted for each season 2017-2024 on the author's own table (the author's files list some seasons' finals first, which lets later-round results reach earlier rows: a look-ahead in the rival's favour).

catboost_lower_tier.about: The same CatBoost recipe given Alcaraz's lower-tier files, 2017-2024 and 2024 alone.

stack.about: yaobviously/tennis_elo's ridge and LightGBM stack with its look-ahead removed, on its own 2017-2023 rows (anchor dates through February 2023).

shipped_catboost_2025.about: The CatBoost the author ships (its checkpoint) and the same recipe refitted through 2024, on 2025.

uts_ingram_derived.about: Ultimate Tennis Statistics and Ingram's point model were not rerun for the current version: their saved forecasts were not restored. On the same 5,270 rows (every 2024-2025 target match) the previous version's log loss reproduces its published value exactly, so the current version minus each rival equals the current version's log loss on those rows minus the rival's published log loss, exact as a point estimate. The interval is a conservative bound, not a bootstrap: the published half-width plus 1.96 times the iid standard error of current minus previous. Every value here is read from the research write-up (write_up), which states the derivation; the published rival and previous-version log losses are also in uts_ingram_2024_2025.json.
uts_ingram_derived.rows: @regex write_up on the same ([0-9,]+) rows \(all 2024–2025 members\)
uts_ingram_derived.previous_log_loss_reproduced: @regex write_up previous version's log loss computes to ([0-9.]+),
uts_ingram_derived.iid_se_current_minus_previous: @regex write_up iid SE of current − previous, ([0-9.]+)\)
uts_ingram_derived.current_minus_uts_bound: @regex write_up \| UTS formula, 2024–2025 \(derived, see below\) \|[^\n]*95% within about (\S+)\)
uts_ingram_derived.current_minus_ingram_bound: @regex write_up \| Ingram's point model, 2024–2025 \(derived\) \|[^\n]*95% within about (\S+)\)
uts_ingram_derived.from_the_inputs: current_log_loss minus the published log loss: UTS {{out:uts_ingram_derived/current_log_loss - out:uts_ingram_derived/uts_published_log_loss|s4}}, Ingram {{out:uts_ingram_derived/current_log_loss - out:uts_ingram_derived/ingram_published_log_loss|s4}}

members.about: Log loss of the average and of each member on every target match (no market price needed). The average scores below both members over 2017-2024 and 2017-2025.

current_vs_previous_unseen.about: The gain over the previous version on seasons never used to build the second model: 2024, 2015-2016 and 2025 (corrected).

calibration_2017_2024.about: Descriptive calibration on 18,888 ATP matches from 2017 to 2024: slope of a no-intercept logistic fit of the outcome on logit(p) (1 is calibrated, below 1 overconfident) and favourite-side bins ten points wide.
